## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/03.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Academic Recovery in 2023
• The availability of 2023 SBA data allows Hawai’i to update
COVID-19 recovery analyses.
• Spring 2023 marks the third year since the pandemic began
and this will be the third report:
• Summer 2021: Academic Impact
• Summer 2022: Academic Recovery Year 1
• Summer 2023: Academic Recovery Year 2</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/04.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Two Types of Recovery: System &amp; Student
• In 2023 we elaborate on the results from the recovery analyses in two
ways:
• System level recovery: Is the education system supporting rates of
learning that are comparable to what it was prior to the pandemic?
• Student level recovery: Are student attaining at levels that are
comparable to what they were prior to the pandemic.
• Previously, we focused mostly on system level recovery: examining rates
of learning in 2021 and 2022 compared to those prior to the pandemic.
• We continue system level analyses but also focus in on student level
recovery.</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/05.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Two Types of Recovery: System &amp; Student
• System level recovery
• Comparison of 2019 and 2023 same grade student growth: We examine
change in baseline student growth (SGPs) for 2019 students and 2023 students
utilizing coefficient matrices derived from pre-pandemic cohorts of students.
• Student level recovery
• Comparison of 2019 to 2023 same grade attainment: We examine equi-
percentile change in attainment for 2019 students and 2023 students.</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/09.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Recovery Phase Year 1
• Student growth (baseline referenced to pre-pandemic rates of learning) was
examined by content area and grade as well as for the major student demographic
subgroups.
• Growth was characterized in three ways:
• Deterioration: Growth less than pre-pandemic rates of learning
• Stabilization: Growth the same as pre-pandemic rates of learning
• Recovery: Growth exceeding pre-pandemic rates of learning
• Because learning slowed during the initial phase of the pandemic, to make up for
those losses, learning must accelerate to rates above normal in order to catch-up
for those loses (recovery).</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/11.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Recovery Year 1
• Analysis of 2022 SBA data indicated several positive trends in Hawai’i to be happy
about.
• In both ELA and mathematics, learning acceleration was at least as much to be
considered stabilization and in many cases could be considered as genuine
recovery.
• Compared to a dozen other states that the Center conducts these analyses,
Hawai’i comes out as the best in terms of pandemic recovery.
• Results from 2023 data will be critical to assess whether these exemplary rates of
learning (beyond what the state experience pre-COVID) are being maintained.</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/14.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Recovery Phase Year 2
• As mentioned previously, we distinguish between student level recovery and
system level recovery this year.
• Because student level recovery utilizes status comparisons between 2019 and
2023 and system level recovery utilizes growth comparisons between 2019 and
2023, status and growth was characterized in three ways:
• Below: Attainment/Growth of students is less in 2023 than in 2019
• Comparable: Attainment/Growth of students is approximately the same in
2023 as in 2019.
• Above: Attainment/Growth of students is greater in 2023 than in 2019</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/18.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Student level recovery
• It is critical to understand that recovery of the system does not imply student level
recovery
• Because students rates of learning slowed so dramatically during the pandemic,
rates of learning necessary to catch students up to where they would have been
would have to be equally dramatic (in the positive direction)
• The following figures illustrate the extent to which student attainment is behind
2019 attainment levels.
• Comparison to 2019 levels is a “low bar” as attainment levels in 2023 had the
pandemic not occurred would almost certainly have been higher than 2019 levels.</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/22.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Recovery Year 2
• In some grades and content areas, student are well behind where their 2019
counterparts were.
• This shows that even though Hawaii’s education system has bounced back well,
large deficits remain to be overcome for thousands of students
• Of particular concern is middle school math, especially for females.</div>
```
